claim: Since 2026-04-09 S3 Lifecycle no longer expires or transitions objects that have failed replication, even if they match a lifecycle rule. When both Replication and Lifecycle are enabled, Lifecycle blocks expiration and transition actions on objects with PENDING or FAILED replication status, and FAILED objects keep incurring storage costs until the replication issue is resolved.

values.display: S3 Lifecycle blocks expiration and transition actions
values.spoken: Lifecycle waits until the object replicates

qualifiers.scope: buckets with both S3 Replication and S3 Lifecycle
qualifiers.condition: applies automatically to existing and new configurations

evidence.quote: When you have both S3 Replication and S3 Lifecycle enabled on a bucket, S3 Lifecycle blocks expiration and transition actions on objects with `PENDING` or `FAILED` replication status.
Objects with `FAILED` replication status will continue to incur storage costs past their Lifecycle expiration or transition eligibility date until the replication issue is resolved.
With this change, S3 Lifecycle no longer expires or transitions objects that have failed replication, even if they match one of the lifecycle rules that you have defined.

claim: AWS positions S3 Files for data that is already in S3 and must be used by file-based applications, AI agents or teams with standard file operations; Amazon EFS for a fully managed shared file system as primary storage where data originates in and is mainly accessed through the file system; and Amazon FSx for existing applications that run on network-attached file storage.

evidence.quote: Use S3 Files when you already have data in S3 and you need file-based applications, AI agents, or teams to work with it directly using standard file operations.
